ai_defects.board: Salandit L34 + Coalossal L28 vs Mega Gyarados + Azumarill, no weather, turn 1 of the battle
ai_defects.chosen: Coalossal chose Protect and Salandit chose Ember at target 3 (its own Coalossal). Protect resolved first and absorbed the friendly Ember.
ai_defects.why_wrong: The authored tactic ACTIVATE SALANDIT EMBER COALOSSAL is the entire concept of this lead. The ally-activation scorer and the Protect scorer do not talk to each other, so the partner's Protect cancels the activation and Salandit's whole turn is thrown away for nothing.
ai_defects.better_action: Either the activation target should not Protect on a turn its partner has selected a friendly activation move, or the activator should see the partner's committed Protect and attack the player instead (Flamethrower on Gyarados / Toxic on Azumarill).

ai_defects.board: Salandit L34 (1 HP, Sash spent) + Coalossal L28 (full) vs Mega Gyarados +1/+1 and Azumarill
ai_defects.chosen: Salandit chose MOVE_FLAMETHROWER at target 3 (its own partner Coalossal).
ai_defects.why_wrong: The dossier picks Ember specifically ('Minimized Special Attack Ember can activate Steam Engine through the quarter-resisted friendly Fire hit; it still costs HP') - Flamethrower is 90 BP against Ember's 40 and costs the partner more than twice the HP for the identical Steam Engine trigger. The activation scorer is not preferring the weakest legal activation move.
ai_defects.better_action: Ember, if the activation is still wanted; otherwise attack the player. (The move never resolved - Aqua Jet KOed Salandit first - but the choice was recorded natively.)

ai_defects.board: Weezing-Galar at 92-99/103, no incoming threat aimed at it
ai_defects.chosen: Protect on three consecutive turns; turn 6 was an outright 'But it failed!'.
ai_defects.why_wrong: Three empty Protects in a row, including one guaranteed failure, while its Mega partner was being focused down. Weezing had Sunny Day (sun had lapsed once) and Will-O-Wisp available and used neither.
ai_defects.better_action: Will-O-Wisp on Azumarill (the Huge Power attacker that was doing all the work), or re-set Sunny Day for the Magmortar/Houndoom payoff.

level_changes.reason: Won on attempt 1 with a single faint; Coalossal is the cheapest non-Mega member and died to one Waterfall without ever getting its Steam Engine turn.
Second-weakest non-Mega member; its High Horsepower was the only reason anything of mine was in danger late, so it is the right place for the other point.

level_change_verification: NOT RERUN. The driver resolves opponent levels out of the prebuilt ROM in work/agent-battle-build-2 and exposes no level override, and this agent is instructed never to run make. The +1s need the main agent's materialize-and-rebuild before they can be re-verified.
could_this_be_cooler: The Steam Engine lead is a great idea that the current shell cannot show off, because Coalossal's own Protect eats the activation and because the payoff (a +6 Speed Coalossal) still has base 30 Speed and a Rock/Fire typing that folds to any Water move at this stage. Two suggestions, neither applied in this pass: (1) give Coalossal Tar Shot or Sandstorm-adjacent support instead of Protect so the activation turn cannot be self-cancelled and the sequencing reads cleanly; (2) let the Steam Engine payoff actually matter by pairing Coalossal with the sun rather than putting Weezing's Sunny Day two slots later - a Salandit that leads with Sunny Day + Ember would make the first two turns of this fight legible as a combo instead of a Protect stall.
authored_set_legality: No legality problems. All six sets were accepted by the native preparation path and every ability, item and move behaved as printed.
